summary.text: Richard Paz is the Democratic candidate for Kansas House of Representatives District 38 in the November 3, 2026 general election, running against incumbent Timothy Johnson (R).
A retired U.S. Army colonel who served from 1987 to 2017, he also ran for the seat in 2024.

paragraphs.text: Paz was born in Tacoma, Washington, and earned a bachelor's degree from the University of Washington in 1987, a graduate degree from Texas A&M University in 2001 and a graduate degree from the Fort Leavenworth School for Advanced Military Studies in 2004, according to Ballotpedia.
He served in the U.S. Army from 1987 to 2017, is retired, and has been affiliated with Rural Leavenworth, Inc.

In a 2024 Ballotpedia survey, he described a 30-year military medical career as a retired Army Medical Service Colonel, with roles including commander, operations officer, planner and educator, and said his work included Army-wide behavioral healthcare planning and teaching at Fort Leavenworth.
Paz ran for Kansas House District 38 in 2024 and lost to incumbent Timothy Johnson (R), 66.4 percent to 33.6 percent; he advanced from the Democratic primary again on August 4, 2026.

In his 2024 survey, he listed property tax reduction and assessment reform, healthcare and childcare affordability, and revenue sharing among his priorities, and said Kansas must approve Medicaid expansion.
